subject: Minimum of the DWLS fit function

messages.author: db5cd54b5422348f
messages.subject: Minimum of the DWLS fit function
parts:
Hi everyone,

I would like to obtain the minimum of the DWLS fit function for my fitted model. In the source code, I saw that the minimum is calculated by lavaan as follows:

diff <- WLS.obs - WLS.est 
group.fx <- sum(diff * diff * WLS.VD) 
group.fx <- 0.5 * (lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]]-1)/lavsamplestats@nobs[[g]] * group.fx

I am aware that lavaan always uses fmin = 0.5*Fmin. However, it is not clear to me why the the minimum is scaled by the sample size. Could you please briefly explain why this is done? Also, can I simply compute 2*group.fx to obtain the textbook Fmin or do I have to account for the scaling factor?

Thank you so much in advance.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Minimum of the DWLS fit function
parts:
I can't speak to the theory behind least-squares fit functions, but I can tell you that in MLE, the minimum fit function is the average (across subjects/cases) log-likelihood ratio under the fitted and saturated models.  The arithmetic mean is a sum divided by the number of things being summed (N), so it follows that the sum is the mean times N.  Thus, the chi-squared statistic (-2 times the log-likelihood ratio of the fitted model relative to the saturated model, which is the sum of such log-likelihood ratios across all N cases) is N times F_ML (the average casewise log-likelihood ratio).  

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
